newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-PIERCE OUSTS SPIRLEA, PHILIPPOUSSIS WITHDRAWS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-PIERCE OUSTS SPIRLEA, PHILIPPOUSSIS WITHDRAWS.

text.p: Former Australian Open champion Mary Pierce ousted fifth seed Irina Spirlea of Romania on Sunday in a first-round upset at a warm-up event for the first Grand Slam of the season.
The Canadian-born, U.S.-based French player defeated Spirlea 6-3 4-6 6-4 on the first day of the Sydney International, the last rehearsal before next week's Australian Open in Melbourne.
But the men's singles lost giant Australian Mark Philippoussis because of tendinitis in his right forearm.
Philippoussis, who beat world number one Pete Sampras at last year's Australian Open, hit with top seed Goran Ivanisevic for 30 minutes in practice on Sunday before the injury forced him off court.
Tournament director Barry Masters said Philippoussis, who ended last year ranked 30th, was advised by doctors not to hit balls for the rest of the week so he can recover for the Australian Open.

Pierce, whose ranking has dropped to 24th, is gradually rediscovering her form after a lingering shoulder injury and was rusty after a three-month layoff. But she still showed some of the power that won her the Open in 1995 as she built up an early 6-3 4-2 lead over the 10th-ranked Spirlea.

But the Romanian baseliner used a fast first serve and unsettling sliced backhand to take the next four games and looked likely to repeat the three-set win she enjoyed over Pierce in the final of a tour event in Florida last April.

The third set began with four successive breaks of service before the two d settled down. Pierce botched an easy smash on her first match point but made no mistake with her second and broke Spirlea's serve to take the final set.
Pierce, 21, said she was still suffering from the shoulder weakness and hoped to use the Sydney tournament to play "a lot of tough matches against a lot of tough girls".

Her second round opponent will be Yayuk Basuki of Indonesia, who defeated Australia's Nicole Bradtke 6-3 3-6 6-0. Bradtke, 27, has also had persistent shoulder problems and said she would decide after the January 13-26 Australian Open whether to continue in the game.
"I don't know what I'm doing or where I'm going," said a dejected Bradtke.
Top women seeds Arantxa Sanchez Vicario, Martina Hingis, Iva Majoli and Lindsay Davenport have all received byes into the second round and are not expected to play before Tuesday.
Ivanisevic is seeded ahead of South Africa's Wayne Ferreira and Spain's Alberto Costa, whose first opponent will be France's Lionel Roux, replacement for Philippoussis in the first round.
